blocks.text: Let's solve this one step by step. What is the smallest whole number that solves four minus x is less than two x plus thirteen?
Add x to both sides, by the addition property of equality. Four is less than three x plus thirteen.
Subtract thirteen from both sides, by the subtraction property. Negative nine is less than three x.
Divide both sides by three, by the division property. Negative three is less than x, so x is greater than negative three. Negative three is not included, so the smallest whole number is negative two.
So the answer is negative two.
Watch out for these traps. If you include the boundary, you get negative three. If you forget to flip the symbol, you get negative four.
